title: A One-Star Spirit Sword
surface: [Fantasy] A woman thinks her changed husband is possessed and buys a spirit-banishing wooden sword. Over the next few days she weakens, while he stays the same. She throws it away and leaves a bad review. The seller visits, banishes a spirit with that very sword, and she removes the review. The sword was never broken. What went wrong?
solution: Both spouses had been possessed without realizing it. Sacred beads first freed the husband, whose return to normal looked wrong to his still-possessed wife. The sword then weakened the spirit inside her, not her already-cured husband. Mistaking this for failure, she discarded it. The visiting seller identified the real remaining host and freed her.

facts.text: The husband had already been freed by sacred beads; his still-possessed wife misread his recovery as possession.
The sword worked on the wife’s spirit all along, and the seller ultimately freed her.
Weakness is part of the fictional supernatural mechanism, not a real medical diagnosis.
The husband neither changed identity nor sabotaged the sword.

unknowns: Names, the spirit’s origin and the price are unspecified.
character_claims: The wife claims her husband is possessed. This is her mistaken diagnosis, not an established fact.
hints: Is the wife’s diagnosis an established fact?
Who actually changes while the sword is present?
The husband is already free; the wife is the remaining possessed person.

source.author: 瑞颜（RuiYanRY）
